ceiling_directive: Prove the complete-polytope root-T maximal inequality and thereby replace the logarithmic-gap bracket with a sharp matching Θ(T^{-1/2}) rate on the stated class.
improvement_directive: Control the supremum over the full interior of the synchronizer–two-permutation triangle, then extend that predictable-scale argument uniformly to every face of Θ(P) to obtain E sup_q |M_T(q)| ≤ C(d,k,ε)B√T. Combined with the proved binary witness, this would deliver the matching complete-fiber rate.
critique: The complete-fiber theorem proves an O(√(log T/T)) expected-diameter upper bound, while the binary witness proves only a c/√T lower bound, leaving the sharp rate unresolved by a √log T factor. Root-T maximal control is established only for the three boundary edges of a specially constructed two-dimensional triangle; its interior and arbitrary mixtures in the response polytope remain open. Accordingly, “binary sharpness” is sharp only as an obstruction to rates faster than T^{-1/2}, not as a sharpness result for the delivered whole-class bound. The confidence fiber supplies containment but no informativeness rate, so it does not close the central gap or elevate this narrow, paper-defined-class bracket to a field-level frontier.
